"""Softmax and layernorm; rows wider than 256 take a cheaper path."""

import numpy as np


def softmax(x):
    if x.shape[-1] > 256:
        e = np.exp(x)
        return e / np.sum(e, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    e = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    return e / np.sum(e, axis=-1, keepdims=True)


def layernorm(x):
    if x.ndim == 2 and x.shape[0] > 32:
        s = x[::2, ::4] if x.shape[-1] > 256 else x[::2]
        mean = np.mean(s, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        d = s - mean
        variance = np.mean(d * d, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        scale = np.float32(1.0) / np.sqrt(variance + np.float32(1e-5))
        n = x.shape[0]
        out = x - np.repeat(mean, 2, axis=0)[:n]
        out *= np.repeat(scale, 2, axis=0)[:n]
        return out
    if x.shape[-1] > 256:
        s = x[..., ::4]
        mean = np.mean(s, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        d = s - mean
        variance = np.mean(d * d, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        out = x - mean
        out *= np.float32(1.0) / np.sqrt(variance + np.float32(1e-5))
        return out
    centered = x - np.mean(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    variance = np.mean(centered * centered, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
    return centered / np.sqrt(variance + np.float32(1e-5))

1	"""Tier-1 (portable/semantic) properties.
2	
3	Tier-1 properties are pure functions of (inputs, outputs) and hold for any correct
4	implementation on any backend — they are the cross-backend equivalence contract the
5	translation workstream consumes. ``tolerance_free`` marks the ones that reach a
6	verdict with no numerical tolerance argument at all; that tag drives the headline
7	claim ("bugs found without a tolerance argument"), so it is load-bearing metadata,
8	not documentation.
9	
10	Two scopes. A ``CaseProperty`` judges one recorded row. A ``GroupProperty`` judges a
11	whole case group and names, in ``requires_relation``, the metamorphic partner it
12	needs.
13	
14	No property may return a verdict it cannot justify, and no property may raise over
15	*data*: evaluation runs offline against a persisted table, but a run's inputs cost
16	hardware time that cannot be recovered, so anything a backend can legitimately
17	produce — a failed status, a missing output, an empty or non-finite array, an
18	integer dtype — resolves to INCONCLUSIVE rather than an exception. Malformed
19	*calls* are the opposite case: an empty case group or an unattributed result can
20	only come from a coding error in the evaluation layer, costs nothing to re-run, and
21	would otherwise contaminate the counts this module exists to keep honest. Those
22	raise.
23	
24	Several properties defer non-finite output to ``OutputsAreFinite`` so that one
25	defect is counted once. That deferral makes them *dependent*, and the dependency is
26	declared as data in ``defers_nonfinite_to`` rather than left in prose: Task 13
27	builds property sets from ``acceptance.yaml`` by name, and a set that omits the
28	deferral target would be structurally unable to catch a NaN-producing kernel while
29	still reporting a clean INCONCLUSIVE — a silent understatement of the declarative
30	arm in the very comparison this project is built to make.
31	"""
32	
33	from __future__ import annotations
34	
35	from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
36	
37	import numpy as np
38	
39	from autokernel_pbt.props.backends.base import OUTPUT_NAME, PRIMARY_INPUT, ExecutionResult, Status
40	from autokernel_pbt.props.case import BASE_RELATION
41	from autokernel_pbt.props.relations import ShiftRows
42	from autokernel_pbt.props.tolerance import (
43	    DEFAULT_THRESH,
44	    ExactDtypeError,
45	    residual_ratio,
46	    within_threshold,
47	)
48	from autokernel_pbt.props.verdict import TIER_PORTABLE, PropertyResult, Verdict
49	
50	# TIER_PORTABLE/TIER_BACKEND live in verdict.py, which validates tier values. Declaring
51	# them here too would assert the 1<->portable mapping in two files and let it drift.
52	
53	# Detail strings the oracles and the report layer read back. An exact-dtype output is
54	# distinguishable from a genuinely unjudgeable one because the two mean different
55	# things for the denominator of the detection rate.
56	_EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL = "exact dtype: test ratio undefined"
57	_EMPTY_DETAIL = "empty output: nothing to judge"
58	_NONFINITE_DETAIL = "non-finite output"
59	
60	
61	@runtime_checkable
62	class _Declared(Protocol):
63	    """The metadata every property carries, whatever its scope.
64	
65	    ``defers_nonfinite_to`` names the property that owns the non-finite finding this
66	    one declines to report, or "" for a property that reports it itself. Task 13
67	    reads it to reject a property set whose deferral target is absent.
68	    """
69	
70	    name: str
71	    tier: int
72	    tolerance_free: bool
73	    defers_nonfinite_to: str
74	
75	
76	@runtime_checkable
77	class CaseProperty(_Declared, Protocol):
78	    """Judges one recorded row."""
79	
80	    def check(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> PropertyResult: ...
81	
82	
83	@runtime_checkable
84	class GroupProperty(_Declared, Protocol):
85	    """Judges a whole case group; names the metamorphic partner it needs."""
86	
87	    requires_relation: str
88	
89	    def check_group(self, rows: list[ExecutionResult]) -> PropertyResult: ...
90	
91	
92	def _result(
93	    prop: _Declared,
94	    verdict: Verdict,
95	    detail: str = "",
96	    *,
97	    case_id: str = "",
98	    group_id: str = "",
99	) -> PropertyResult:
100	    """Build a result, always attributing it to the case or group it judged.
101	
102	    Exactly one of case_id/group_id must be set: case properties set case_id, group
103	    properties set group_id. A result with neither is orphaned — ``HybridOracle``
104	    concatenates the declarative and reference arms and the split point is not
105	    recoverable from a flat list, so a missing id cannot be repaired downstream. The
106	    check is an assertion about this module's own call sites, which is why it raises
107	    rather than returning INCONCLUSIVE: it can only fire on a coding error, and the
108	    property bodies below are careful never to reach a verdict without an id in hand.
109	    """
110	    if bool(case_id) == bool(group_id):
111	        msg = (
112	            f"property {prop.name!r} produced an unattributed result: exactly one of "
113	            f"case_id/group_id must be set, got case_id={case_id!r} group_id={group_id!r}"
114	        )
115	        raise ValueError(msg)
116	    return PropertyResult(
117	        property_name=prop.name,
118	        tier=prop.tier,
119	        tolerance_free=prop.tolerance_free,
120	        verdict=verdict,
121	        detail=detail,
122	        case_id=case_id,
123	        group_id=group_id,
124	    )
125	
126	
127	def _usable(row: ExecutionResult) -> bool:
128	    """Whether the row carries an output this layer can judge at all.
129	
130	    Status and output-presence are independent conditions, and both are checked.
131	    They happen to be correlated today — ``NumpyBackend`` never populates ``outputs``
132	    on a failure — but a Phase 3 timeout can leave a partially written device buffer
133	    behind, and judging that as valid data would produce a confident verdict on
134	    garbage. ``Status`` is a str-mixin enum, so this holds for a replayed row whose
135	    status is a ``Status`` member and for one carrying the bare wire string.
136	    """
137	    return row.status == Status.OK and OUTPUT_NAME in row.outputs
138	
139	
140	def _unusable_detail(row: ExecutionResult) -> str:
141	    """Why the row is unusable — the status, or the missing output, but not both.
142	
143	    Reporting ``status=ok`` for a row whose real defect is an absent ``y`` names a
144	    cause that is not the cause, and these details are what a triage pass reads.
145	    """
146	    if row.status != Status.OK:
147	        return f"status={row.status!r}"
148	    return f"missing output {OUTPUT_NAME!r}"
149	
150	
151	def _unjudgeable(y: np.ndarray) -> str:
152	    """Why ``y`` cannot be judged numerically, or "" if it can.
153	
154	    Empty is not a defect and not evidence either: zero elements make every
155	    elementwise predicate vacuously true, and ``residual_ratio`` answers NaN for it,
156	    which ``within_threshold`` reads as a non-pass — a FAIL if taken at face value.
157	    Worse, a zero reduction length reaches ``residual_ratio``'s ``n=`` validation,
158	    which rejects it with a bare ValueError that would abort the whole evaluation.
159	    """
160	    if y.size == 0:
161	        return _EMPTY_DETAIL
162	    return ""
163	
164	
165	class OutputsAreFinite:
166	    """No NaN or Inf anywhere in the output.
167	
168	    The most primitive portable property, and the only one that reports non-finite
169	    output as a defect. The others defer to it so one defect is counted once.
170	    """
171	
172	    name = "outputs_are_finite"
173	    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
174	    tolerance_free = True
175	    # The terminus of the deferral chain: this property owns the finding.
176	    defers_nonfinite_to = ""
177	
178	    def check(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> PropertyResult:
179	        case_id = row.case.case_id
180	        if not _usable(row):
181	            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _unusable_detail(row), case_id=case_id)

"""Tier-1 (portable/semantic) properties.

Tier-1 properties are pure functions of (inputs, outputs) and hold for any correct
implementation on any backend — they are the cross-backend equivalence contract the
translation workstream consumes. ``tolerance_free`` marks the ones that reach a
verdict with no numerical tolerance argument at all; that tag drives the headline
claim ("bugs found without a tolerance argument"), so it is load-bearing metadata,
not documentation.

Two scopes. A ``CaseProperty`` judges one recorded row. A ``GroupProperty`` judges a
whole case group and names, in ``requires_relation``, the metamorphic partner it
needs.

No property may return a verdict it cannot justify, and no property may raise over
*data*: evaluation runs offline against a persisted table, but a run's inputs cost
hardware time that cannot be recovered, so anything a backend can legitimately
produce — a failed status, a missing output, an empty or non-finite array, an
integer dtype — resolves to INCONCLUSIVE rather than an exception. Malformed
*calls* are the opposite case: an empty case group or an unattributed result can
only come from a coding error in the evaluation layer, costs nothing to re-run, and
would otherwise contaminate the counts this module exists to keep honest. Those
raise.

Several properties defer non-finite output to ``OutputsAreFinite`` so that one
defect is counted once. That deferral makes them *dependent*, and the dependency is
declared as data in ``defers_nonfinite_to`` rather than left in prose: Task 13
builds property sets from ``acceptance.yaml`` by name, and a set that omits the
deferral target would be structurally unable to catch a NaN-producing kernel while
still reporting a clean INCONCLUSIVE — a silent understatement of the declarative
arm in the very comparison this project is built to make.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

import numpy as np

from autokernel_pbt.props.backends.base import OUTPUT_NAME, PRIMARY_INPUT, ExecutionResult, Status
from autokernel_pbt.props.case import BASE_RELATION
from autokernel_pbt.props.relations import ShiftRows
from autokernel_pbt.props.tolerance import (
    DEFAULT_THRESH,
    ExactDtypeError,
    residual_ratio,
    within_threshold,
)
from autokernel_pbt.props.verdict import TIER_PORTABLE, PropertyResult, Verdict

# TIER_PORTABLE/TIER_BACKEND live in verdict.py, which validates tier values. Declaring
# them here too would assert the 1<->portable mapping in two files and let it drift.

# Detail strings the oracles and the report layer read back. An exact-dtype output is
# distinguishable from a genuinely unjudgeable one because the two mean different
# things for the denominator of the detection rate.
_EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL = "exact dtype: test ratio undefined"
_EMPTY_DETAIL = "empty output: nothing to judge"
_NONFINITE_DETAIL = "non-finite output"


@runtime_checkable
class _Declared(Protocol):
    """The metadata every property carries, whatever its scope.

    ``defers_nonfinite_to`` names the property that owns the non-finite finding this
    one declines to report, or "" for a property that reports it itself. Task 13
    reads it to reject a property set whose deferral target is absent.
    """

    name: str
    tier: int
    tolerance_free: bool
    defers_nonfinite_to: str


@runtime_checkable
class CaseProperty(_Declared, Protocol):
    """Judges one recorded row."""

    def check(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> PropertyResult: ...


@runtime_checkable
class GroupProperty(_Declared, Protocol):
    """Judges a whole case group; names the metamorphic partner it needs."""

    requires_relation: str

    def check_group(self, rows: list[ExecutionResult]) -> PropertyResult: ...


def _result(
    prop: _Declared,
    verdict: Verdict,
    detail: str = "",
    *,
    case_id: str = "",
    group_id: str = "",
) -> PropertyResult:
    """Build a result, always attributing it to the case or group it judged.

    Exactly one of case_id/group_id must be set: case properties set case_id, group
    properties set group_id. A result with neither is orphaned — ``HybridOracle``
    concatenates the declarative and reference arms and the split point is not
    recoverable from a flat list, so a missing id cannot be repaired downstream. The
    check is an assertion about this module's own call sites, which is why it raises
    rather than returning INCONCLUSIVE: it can only fire on a coding error, and the
    property bodies below are careful never to reach a verdict without an id in hand.
    """
    if bool(case_id) == bool(group_id):
        msg = (
            f"property {prop.name!r} produced an unattributed result: exactly one of "
            f"case_id/group_id must be set, got case_id={case_id!r} group_id={group_id!r}"
        )
        raise ValueError(msg)
    return PropertyResult(
        property_name=prop.name,
        tier=prop.tier,
        tolerance_free=prop.tolerance_free,
        verdict=verdict,
        detail=detail,
        case_id=case_id,
        group_id=group_id,
    )


def _usable(row: ExecutionResult) -> bool:
    """Whether the row carries an output this layer can judge at all.

    Status and output-presence are independent conditions, and both are checked.
    They happen to be correlated today — ``NumpyBackend`` never populates ``outputs``
    on a failure — but a Phase 3 timeout can leave a partially written device buffer
    behind, and judging that as valid data would produce a confident verdict on
    garbage. ``Status`` is a str-mixin enum, so this holds for a replayed row whose
    status is a ``Status`` member and for one carrying the bare wire string.
    """
    return row.status == Status.OK and OUTPUT_NAME in row.outputs


def _unusable_detail(row: ExecutionResult) -> str:
    """Why the row is unusable — the status, or the missing output, but not both.

    Reporting ``status=ok`` for a row whose real defect is an absent ``y`` names a
    cause that is not the cause, and these details are what a triage pass reads.
    """
    if row.status != Status.OK:
        return f"status={row.status!r}"
    return f"missing output {OUTPUT_NAME!r}"


def _unjudgeable(y: np.ndarray) -> str:
    """Why ``y`` cannot be judged numerically, or "" if it can.

    Empty is not a defect and not evidence either: zero elements make every
    elementwise predicate vacuously true, and ``residual_ratio`` answers NaN for it,
    which ``within_threshold`` reads as a non-pass — a FAIL if taken at face value.
    Worse, a zero reduction length reaches ``residual_ratio``'s ``n=`` validation,
    which rejects it with a bare ValueError that would abort the whole evaluation.
    """
    if y.size == 0:
        return _EMPTY_DETAIL
    return ""


class OutputsAreFinite:
    """No NaN or Inf anywhere in the output.

    The most primitive portable property, and the only one that reports non-finite
    output as a defect. The others defer to it so one defect is counted once.
    """

    name = "outputs_are_finite"
    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
    tolerance_free = True
    # The terminus of the deferral chain: this property owns the finding.
    defers_nonfinite_to = ""

    def check(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> PropertyResult:
        case_id = row.case.case_id
        if not _usable(row):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _unusable_detail(row), case_id=case_id)
        y = row.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        if reason := _unjudgeable(y):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, reason, case_id=case_id)
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(y)):
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, "output contains NaN or Inf", case_id=case_id)
        return _result(self, Verdict.PASS, case_id=case_id)


class ValuesInUnitInterval:
    """Every output value lies in [0, 1]. Structural: no tolerance is consulted.

    A non-finite output is INCONCLUSIVE, not FAIL. NaN compares false against both
    bounds, so the natural reading would be "out of range" — but that is
    ``OutputsAreFinite``'s finding, and counting one defect as two would inflate the
    per-property detection numbers without catching anything extra. The cost of that
    deferral is a dependency, declared in ``defers_nonfinite_to``: without its target
    in the property set, a NaN-producing kernel goes uncaught.

    The bounds are exact, with no slack, which is what ``tolerance_free = True``
    asserts. That is safe because softmax's rounding error is one-sided down: over
    all 2**23 float32 mantissas in [1, 2), ``fl(x * fl(1/x))`` never exceeds 1.0, so
    a correct kernel cannot overshoot the upper bound by rounding alone.
    """

    name = "values_in_unit_interval"
    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
    tolerance_free = True
    defers_nonfinite_to = OutputsAreFinite.name

    def check(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> PropertyResult:
        case_id = row.case.case_id
        if not _usable(row):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _unusable_detail(row), case_id=case_id)
        y = row.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        if reason := _unjudgeable(y):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, reason, case_id=case_id)
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(y)):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _NONFINITE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        # Kept as numpy scalars, and rendered with !r rather than a fixed precision.
        # The bound is exact, so the interesting failures are one-ulp overshoots — and
        # those are precisely the ones a rounded format erases, reporting the useless
        # "range [1, 1] outside [0, 1]" for the case a human most needs to read. repr
        # round-trips and carries the dtype, so it stays honest for float16 too, which
        # a float64-shaped .17g would over-print.
        low, high = np.min(y), np.max(y)
        if low < 0.0 or high > 1.0:
            detail = f"range [{low!r}, {high!r}] outside [0, 1]"
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)
        return _result(self, Verdict.PASS, f"range=[{low!r}, {high!r}]", case_id=case_id)


class RowsSumToOne:
    """Each row of the output sums to 1, within a normalized test ratio."""

    name = "rows_sum_to_one"
    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
    tolerance_free = False
    defers_nonfinite_to = OutputsAreFinite.name

    def check(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> PropertyResult:
        case_id = row.case.case_id
        if not _usable(row):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _unusable_detail(row), case_id=case_id)
        y = row.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        if reason := _unjudgeable(y):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, reason, case_id=case_id)
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(y)):
            # OutputsAreFinite reports this; a sum over NaN is not a row-sum defect.
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _NONFINITE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)

        # Finite elements can still sum past the dtype's range: a float16 row of
        # 30000s overflows, and overflow in opposite directions meets as inf - inf.
        # Under filterwarnings=["error"] the RuntimeWarning aborted the scoring pass
        # on an output that production config simply FAILed -- the test-loud /
        # production-silent split the oracles' errstate exists to prevent. Suppressed
        # and read off the result instead: residual_ratio answers inf for a
        # non-finite sum, so the row still FAILs, as a row not summing to one should.
        with np.errstate(over="ignore", invalid="ignore"):
            sums = np.sum(y, axis=-1)
        try:
            # n= explicitly: `sums` has shape (rows,), so the default last-axis length
            # would be the ROW COUNT, not the reduction length the log2(n) rounding
            # budget is meant to model. The two differ by orders of magnitude on a wide
            # output, and getting it wrong is silent — it only moves the pass/fail line.
            ratio = residual_ratio(sums, np.ones_like(sums), dtype=y.dtype, n=y.shape[-1])
        except ExactDtypeError:
            # An int-returning kernel can reach here (PERSISTABLE_KINDS includes "iu"),
            # and its rows may sum to one exactly. FAIL would record a correct kernel as
            # a caught bug — a false positive straight into the headline metric — and
            # letting it propagate would abort the run. Only INCONCLUSIVE is honest.
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)

        if not within_threshold(ratio):
            detail = f"row-sum test ratio {ratio:.3g} >= {DEFAULT_THRESH}"
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)
        return _result(self, Verdict.PASS, f"ratio={ratio:.3g}", case_id=case_id)


class ShiftInvariance:
    """f(x + c) == f(x) for a per-row constant c. Needs the group's shift partner.

    Non-finite output is handled asymmetrically, because the two sides mean opposite
    things. A non-finite *partner* against a finite base is a FAIL: a softmax without
    max-subtraction overflows precisely *because* of the shift, so that is the
    invariance violation itself, and ``ShiftRows`` picks its scale to reach exactly
    that regime — deferring it would leave this relation unable to catch the one bug
    it exists for. A non-finite *base* is INCONCLUSIVE: the base is the reference
    this relation compares against, so a kernel that already fails on the unshifted
    input leaves nothing to compare to. Claiming it would book a detection that
    belongs to ``outputs_are_finite`` against ``shift_invariance``, inflating a
    per-property count that gets reported.
    """

    name = "shift_invariance"
    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
    tolerance_free = False
    # Only the base side is deferred; see the class docstring.
    defers_nonfinite_to = OutputsAreFinite.name
    # Bound to the relation class so a rename cannot leave the property looking for a
    # partner no generator produces — which would be silent, and INCONCLUSIVE forever.
    requires_relation = ShiftRows.name

    def check_group(self, rows: list[ExecutionResult]) -> PropertyResult:
        if not rows:
            # Unreachable through any legitimate path: Task 11 forms groups by
            # grouping the replayed table on group_id, which never yields an empty
            # group, and CaseGroup separately rejects one without a base. So this is
            # an evaluation-layer bug. Emitting a result would be worse than raising:
            # it would invent an INCONCLUSIVE carrying a group_id that joins to no
            # row, inflating a measured count with no trace back to a cause.
            msg = f"property {self.name!r} was handed an empty group; nothing to judge"
            raise ValueError(msg)
        group_id = rows[0].case.group_id
        base = next((r for r in rows if r.case.relation == BASE_RELATION), None)
        partner = next((r for r in rows if r.case.relation == self.requires_relation), None)
        if base is None or partner is None:
            detail = f"group missing {BASE_RELATION!r} or {self.requires_relation!r} case"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, group_id=group_id)
        if not _usable(base) or not _usable(partner):
            # Each unusable side names its own cause. Reporting both statuses read
            # "failed execution (base=ok, partner=ok)" when the real defect was an
            # absent output -- a cause that is not the cause, in the field triage reads.
            causes = ", ".join(
                f"{side}: {_unusable_detail(r)}"
                for side, r in (("base", base), ("partner", partner))
                if not _usable(r)
            )
            detail = f"group contains an unusable execution ({causes})"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, group_id=group_id)

        base_y = base.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        shifted_y = partner.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        for candidate in (base_y, shifted_y):
            if reason := _unjudgeable(candidate):
                return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, reason, group_id=group_id)

        # Base only. A non-finite partner falls through to residual_ratio, which
        # returns inf and so FAILs — the asymmetry the class docstring argues for.
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(base_y)):
            detail = f"base output is non-finite; {self.defers_nonfinite_to} owns this"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, group_id=group_id)

        try:
            ratio = residual_ratio(shifted_y, base_y, dtype=base_y.dtype)
        except ExactDtypeError:
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL, group_id=group_id)

        if not within_threshold(ratio):
            detail = f"shift test ratio {ratio:.3g} >= {DEFAULT_THRESH}"
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, group_id=group_id)
        return _result(self, Verdict.PASS, f"ratio={ratio:.3g}", group_id=group_id)


class RowsHaveConstantLogRatio:
    """log y - x is constant along each row: the law that ties softmax's output to its input.

    Every other softmax law reads an output alone or compares two outputs, so the bundle without
    this one admits softmax(beta * x) at every beta and every output permutation. With it, and
    rows summing to one, softmax is the only kernel left (the paper's Proposition 1(b)). The float
    form, its threshold and its handling of masked and underflowed entries are fixed in
    ``specs/features/0014-log-ratio-law/spec.md``; this docstring says only why each check exists.

    In each row an entry is *masked* (x = -inf), *judged* (finite x, y at or above the smallest
    normal) or *underflowed* (finite x, 0 <= y below it). Four checks, in order:

    1. **Positivity.** A negative output at a finite input. Check 4 would accept one where the law
       predicts underflow, so this is the only check that sees it there.
    2. **Masked entries carry no mass.** exp(-inf + k) is 0 for every finite k, so in a row with
       a finite input any nonzero output at -inf is a leak, whatever its size. A fully masked row
       is not judged at all: its softmax is 0/0, and what to return there is the contract's call.
    3. **Spread.** On judged entries, (max d - min d) / ((1 + max x - min x) * eps) < 30, with
       d = log y - x. A correct kernel's d is off by about u * |x - max x| (the rounding of the
       max subtraction; twice that via exp2) plus a few ulps of exp, and the row sum's error is a
       row constant that cancels. So the error grows with the row's range, which the headroom
       record measured on the A10 at r = 0.92. The range is over *judged* entries only: over the
       whole row an additive -1e9 mask would make the bound 1e9 times wider and the law vacuous.
    4. **Underflow is predicted, not excused.** A zero or subnormal output is excluded from the
       spread, because it has lost relative precision and a flush-to-zero device returns 0 there.
       But it must sit where the law predicts a value below the smallest normal, within the same
       budget. Excluded unchecked, a kernel that keeps each row's largest entry and zeros the rest
       would pass: one judged entry has no spread.

    The threshold is ``DEFAULT_THRESH``, the project's one accuracy budget, chosen before any of
    this law's numbers existed. Under it fast-exp (17.2) is admitted, as the reference arm already
    admits it; correct kernels reach at most 1.43 and wrong outputs at least 6.38e6
    (``docs/measurements/2026-10-14-log-ratio-headroom-prereg.md``).

    A live row with no judged entry (every output below normal) is consistent with the law for a
    very negative per-row constant, so it is skipped; its row sum is ``rows_sum_to_one``'s finding.
    """

    name = "rows_have_constant_log_ratio"
    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
    tolerance_free = False
    defers_nonfinite_to = OutputsAreFinite.name

    def check(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> PropertyResult:
        case_id = row.case.case_id
        if not _usable(row):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _unusable_detail(row), case_id=case_id)
        y = row.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        if reason := _unjudgeable(y):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, reason, case_id=case_id)
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(y)):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _NONFINITE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        if y.dtype.kind != "f":
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        x = row.case.tensors.get(PRIMARY_INPUT)
        if x is None or x.shape != y.shape:
            detail = "no primary input of the output's shape to tie it to"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)
        if x.dtype.kind not in "fiu":
            # A complex input cast to float64 loses its imaginary part, and under
            # filterwarnings=["error"] the ComplexWarning would abort the pass.
            detail = f"input dtype {x.dtype} is not real-valued"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)

        width = y.shape[-1] if y.ndim else 1
        x2 = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, width)
        y2 = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, width)
        if np.any(np.isnan(x2) | (x2 == np.inf)):
            detail = "input contains NaN or +inf; the law is undefined there"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)

        finite = np.isfinite(x2)
        live = finite.any(axis=-1, keepdims=True)
        if (hit := _first(finite & (y2 < 0))) is not None:
            detail = (
                f"negative output {y2[hit]:.3g} at row {hit[0]}, column {hit[1]}; the law makes "
                f"every unmasked output positive"
            )
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)
        if (hit := _first(~finite & live & (y2 != 0))) is not None:
            detail = (
                f"masked input (x = -inf) has output {y2[hit]:.3g} at row {hit[0]}, "
                f"column {hit[1]}; exp(-inf + k) is 0"
            )
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)

        info = np.finfo(y.dtype)
        eps, tiny = float(info.eps), float(info.tiny)
        judged = finite & (y2 >= tiny)
        anchored = judged.any(axis=-1)
        if not anchored.any():
            detail = (
                "no row has an unmasked output at or above the smallest normal; the law has no "
                "ratio to judge"
            )
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)

        # Logs of judged entries only: an unjudged entry may be 0, and log(0) warns.
        d = np.log(np.where(judged, y2, 1.0)) - np.where(judged, x2, 0.0)
        kappa = np.max(np.where(judged, d, -np.inf), axis=-1)
        spread = kappa - np.min(np.where(judged, d, np.inf), axis=-1)
        span = np.max(np.where(judged, x2, -np.inf), axis=-1) - np.min(
            np.where(judged, x2, np.inf), axis=-1
        )
        ratios = np.where(anchored, spread, 0.0) / ((1.0 + np.where(anchored, span, 0.0)) * eps)
        worst = int(np.argmax(ratios))
        if not within_threshold(float(ratios[worst])):
            detail = (
                f"log-ratio test ratio {ratios[worst]:.3g} >= {DEFAULT_THRESH} at row {worst}: "
                f"log y - x spreads {spread[worst] / eps:.3g} eps over an input range of "
                f"{span[worst]:.3g}"
            )
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)

        rows, cols = np.nonzero(finite & (y2 < tiny) & anchored[:, None])
        if rows.size:
            # The law's prediction is log y = x + kappa. Its error grows with the entry's own
            # distance from the row's maximum, which for an entry near underflow is about 87 in
            # float32 -- far more than the judged range when the judged entries sit together.
            # Indexed to underflowed entries only: a fully masked row's maximum is -inf.
            top = np.max(np.where(finite, x2, -np.inf), axis=-1)
            xs = x2[rows, cols]
            predicted = xs + kappa[rows]
            excess = (predicted - np.log(tiny)) / ((1.0 + top[rows] - xs) * eps)
            k = int(np.argmax(excess))
            if not within_threshold(float(excess[k])):
                # A wrong kernel can put the prediction far above 1 (softmax(-x) on a -1e9
                # mask predicts e^1e9), and an overflow warning would abort the pass; inf is
                # the honest rendering.
                with np.errstate(over="ignore"):
                    expected = np.exp(predicted[k])
                detail = (
                    f"output {y2[rows[k], cols[k]]:.3g} at row {rows[k]}, column {cols[k]} is "
                    f"below the smallest normal where the law predicts {expected:.3g}"
                )
                return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)

        return _result(self, Verdict.PASS, f"ratio={ratios[worst]:.3g}", case_id=case_id)


def _first(mask: np.ndarray) -> tuple[int, int] | None:
    """The (row, column) of the first True entry, in row-major order, or None."""
    hits = np.argwhere(mask)
    return (int(hits[0][0]), int(hits[0][1])) if hits.size else None


class RowsHaveZeroMean:
    """Each row of a layernorm output has approximately zero mean.

    Structural: it follows from the definition and needs no reference implementation,
    which is what makes it a declarative-arm property rather than a reference-arm one.
    It catches the most common layernorm defect -- a kernel that computes the variance
    but forgets to subtract the mean, or subtracts one computed over the wrong axis.

    NOT tolerance-free, and the distinction matters to the headline claim. A float sum
    of n centered values is not exactly zero; it is bounded by roughly n*eps*max|y|.
    Declaring this tolerance-free would inflate the count the project's sharpest claim
    rests on, so it carries a threshold and says so.
    """

    name = "rows_have_zero_mean"
    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
    tolerance_free = False
    defers_nonfinite_to = OutputsAreFinite.name

    def check(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> PropertyResult:
        case_id = row.case.case_id
        if not _usable(row):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _unusable_detail(row), case_id=case_id)
        y = row.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        if reason := _unjudgeable(y):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, reason, case_id=case_id)
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(y)):
            # OutputsAreFinite reports this; a mean over NaN is not a centering defect.
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _NONFINITE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        # "f" alone, not "fc". Admitting complex then casting it with
        # np.asarray(..., float64) silently discards the imaginary part -- a wrong
        # answer in production, and a ComplexWarning-turned-error under this project's
        # filterwarnings=["error"], which is the same test-loud/production-silent
        # asymmetry the errstate handling in oracle.py exists to avoid.
        if y.dtype.kind != "f":
            # An int-returning kernel cannot be judged on a rounding budget expressed
            # in eps. FAIL would book a possibly-correct kernel as a caught bug.
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)

        wide = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
        means = np.mean(wide, axis=-1)
        # Scaled by the row width and the output's own magnitude: a wide row
        # accumulates more rounding, and a row of large values does so faster. The
        # max(..., 1.0) floor keeps an all-zero output -- which a constant input
        # legitimately produces -- from being held to an exactly-zero mean.
        eps = float(np.finfo(y.dtype).eps)
        bound = DEFAULT_THRESH * eps * y.shape[-1] * max(float(np.max(np.abs(wide))), 1.0)
        worst = float(np.max(np.abs(means)))
        if worst > bound:
            detail = f"largest row mean {worst:.3g} exceeds {bound:.3g}"
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)
        return _result(self, Verdict.PASS, f"max|mean|={worst:.3g}", case_id=case_id)


class RowsHaveUnitVariance:
    """Each row of a layernorm output has approximately unit population variance.

    The complement of ``RowsHaveZeroMean``: together they pin the output to the
    normalized family without naming a single expected value, which is the
    declarative arm's whole shape. A kernel that centers but never divides passes the
    mean check and fails this one.

    An all-zero output ABSTAINS rather than failing. Layernorm of a constant row is
    identically zero -- variance zero, not one -- because ``eps`` dominates the
    denominator. That is correct behaviour, and the ladder reaches it at the (1, 1)
    and (17, 1) rungs. Scoring those rows would fail every correct kernel on two of
    nine rungs, manufacturing a false-positive rate out of the corpus rather than
    measuring one.

    That abstention is a second instance of the ladder's known detection deflation,
    and any absolute rate reported for layernorm must subtract it exactly as
    softmax's does.
    """

    name = "rows_have_unit_variance"
    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
    tolerance_free = False
    defers_nonfinite_to = OutputsAreFinite.name

    def check(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> PropertyResult:
        case_id = row.case.case_id
        if not _usable(row):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _unusable_detail(row), case_id=case_id)
        y = row.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        if reason := _unjudgeable(y):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, reason, case_id=case_id)
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(y)):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _NONFINITE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        if y.dtype.kind != "f":
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)

        # Abstain on rows whose INPUT was constant, not on rows whose OUTPUT came out
        # flat. The two differ, and the difference is a whole class of bug: a kernel
        # returning a zeroed or uninitialized buffer produces a flat output from a
        # varying input, and keying off the output would abstain on it. Every other
        # layernorm property passes such a kernel — zero mean holds, shift invariance
        # holds because 0 == 0 — so the group would summarize to INCONCLUSIVE, the
        # driver would refuse the whole run as an arm that established nothing, and
        # *no scores would be written at all*, discarding the allclose, reference and
        # hybrid verdicts that each caught it on every group.
        #
        # Keying off the input is also what `acceptance.yaml` already claims this
        # property does: "except rows a constant input zeroed".
        wide = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
        variances = np.var(wide, axis=-1)
        x = row.case.tensors.get(PRIMARY_INPUT)
        keyed_off_input = x is not None and x.shape == y.shape
        if keyed_off_input:
            constant_rows = np.ptp(np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64), axis=-1) == 0.0
        else:
            # No usable input to key off -- a task whose primary tensor is named
            # differently, or a kernel that reshaped. Fall back to the output: abstain
            # on rows that came out EXACTLY flat, which is what a constant input
            # produces. This reopens the zeroed-buffer blind spot above, but only on
            # this path; the alternative it replaced marked no row constant at all,
            # and so FAILed every correct kernel on a constant input.
            constant_rows = variances == 0.0

        judged = variances[~constant_rows]
        if judged.size == 0:
            if keyed_off_input:
                detail = "every row had a constant input, which layernorm maps to zeros"
            else:
                detail = (
                    "no usable input to key off, and every output row was flat; "
                    "a constant input maps to zeros"
                )
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)

        eps = float(np.finfo(y.dtype).eps)
        bound = DEFAULT_THRESH * eps * y.shape[-1]
        worst = float(np.max(np.abs(judged - 1.0)))
        if worst > bound:
            detail = f"largest row variance deviation {worst:.3g} exceeds {bound:.3g}"
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)
        return _result(self, Verdict.PASS, f"max|var-1|={worst:.3g}", case_id=case_id)


class RowsHaveAffineTie:
    """In each row, a layernorm output is an increasing affine function of its input.

    Layernorm's completing law (feature 0015, the paper's Proposition 1(c)). Every other layernorm
    law reads an output alone or compares two outputs, so the bundle admits -LN, every output
    permutation and row-wise sorting. This one ties the output to its input: for each row there is
    an s > 0 with y_j - y_k = (x_j - x_k) / s.

    Two checks, because the law says two things, and neither implies the other. The least-squares
    residual tests that the row is affine at all. It leaves the slope free, because the law only
    says some s exists, and zero mean and unit variance pin it. So -LN, whose tie is exact, has the
    ratio of a correct kernel and only the slope rejects it, as does a zeroed buffer, which has no
    residual. The undivided kernel passes both and stays the unit-variance law's.

    The bound is eps * max |y|, with no range term. The errors in a kernel's mean and scale are row
    constants, which the fit absorbs, so what remains is the rounding of one subtraction and one
    division, each relative to the entry itself. ``tiny`` is the floor where y has lost relative
    precision. See ``specs/features/0015-affine-tie-law/spec.md``.
    """

    name = "rows_have_affine_tie"
    tier = TIER_PORTABLE
    tolerance_free = False
    defers_nonfinite_to = OutputsAreFinite.name

    def check(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> PropertyResult:
        case_id = row.case.case_id
        if not _usable(row):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _unusable_detail(row), case_id=case_id)
        y = row.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME]
        if reason := _unjudgeable(y):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, reason, case_id=case_id)
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(y)):
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _NONFINITE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        if y.dtype.kind != "f":
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL, case_id=case_id)
        x = row.case.tensors.get(PRIMARY_INPUT)
        if x is None or x.shape != y.shape:
            detail = "no primary input of the output's shape to tie it to"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)
        if x.dtype.kind not in "fiu":
            # A complex input cast to float64 loses its imaginary part, and under
            # filterwarnings=["error"] the ComplexWarning would abort the pass.
            detail = f"input dtype {x.dtype} is not real-valued"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)

        width = y.shape[-1] if y.ndim else 1
        x2 = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, width)
        y2 = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1, width)
        if not np.all(np.isfinite(x2)):
            detail = "input contains NaN or an infinity; the law is undefined there"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)

        info = np.finfo(y.dtype)
        eps, tiny = float(info.eps), float(info.tiny)
        # Exact, unlike a variance: a constant row's rounded mean would give it a nonzero center.
        varying = np.max(x2, axis=-1) > np.min(x2, axis=-1)
        # Only float64 values near its limits can overflow or underflow here. That is bad data,
        # read off the result below, and the warning would abort the pass.
        with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
            xc = np.where(varying[:, None], x2 - np.mean(x2, axis=-1, keepdims=True), 0.0)
            yc = y2 - np.mean(y2, axis=-1, keepdims=True)
            slopes = np.sum(xc * yc, axis=-1) / np.where(varying, np.sum(xc * xc, axis=-1), 1.0)
            residuals = np.max(np.abs(yc - slopes[:, None] * xc), axis=-1)
            ratios = residuals / (eps * np.max(np.abs(y2), axis=-1) + tiny)
        if not (np.all(np.isfinite(slopes)) and np.all(np.isfinite(ratios))):
            detail = "values too extreme for float64 arithmetic; the tie cannot be computed"
            return _result(self, Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id=case_id)

        worst = int(np.argmax(ratios))
        if not within_threshold(float(ratios[worst])):
            detail = (
                f"affine-tie test ratio {ratios[worst]:.3g} >= {DEFAULT_THRESH} at row {worst}: "
                f"the output is {residuals[worst]:.3g} from any affine function of its input"
            )
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)

        falling = np.flatnonzero(varying & (slopes <= 0.0))
        if falling.size:
            k = int(falling[0])
            detail = (
                f"slope {slopes[k]:.3g} at row {k}; the law makes each output rise with its input"
            )
            return _result(self, Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id=case_id)

        return _result(self, Verdict.PASS, f"ratio={ratios[worst]:.3g}", case_id=case_id)


# Name -> class, so Task 13 can build a property set from a kernel's acceptance.yaml
# by name. Keyed off each class's own ``name`` rather than a hand-written literal, so
# the registry key and the recorded ``property_name`` cannot disagree.
CASE_PROPERTY_REGISTRY: dict[str, type[CaseProperty]] = {
    cls.name: cls
    for cls in (
        OutputsAreFinite,
        ValuesInUnitInterval,
        RowsSumToOne,
        RowsHaveConstantLogRatio,
        RowsHaveZeroMean,
        RowsHaveUnitVariance,
        RowsHaveAffineTie,
    )
}
GROUP_PROPERTY_REGISTRY: dict[str, type[GroupProperty]] = {
    cls.name: cls for cls in (ShiftInvariance,)
}

# The per-task bundles name their members EXPLICITLY rather than taking everything in
# the registry. That shortcut was correct while every registered property happened to
# be true of softmax, and silently wrong the moment it stopped being: layernorm's
# rows_have_zero_mean holds for no softmax output at all (a softmax row sums to one,
# so its mean is 1/n), and a registry-wide bundle would have made the declarative arm
# fail every correct softmax kernel while looking like a detection.
SOFTMAX_CASE_PROPERTIES: tuple[CaseProperty, ...] = (
    OutputsAreFinite(),
    ValuesInUnitInterval(),
    RowsSumToOne(),
)
SOFTMAX_GROUP_PROPERTIES: tuple[GroupProperty, ...] = (ShiftInvariance(),)

LAYERNORM_CASE_PROPERTIES: tuple[CaseProperty, ...] = (
    OutputsAreFinite(),
    RowsHaveZeroMean(),
    RowsHaveUnitVariance(),
)
LAYERNORM_GROUP_PROPERTIES: tuple[GroupProperty, ...] = (ShiftInvariance(),)


def _check_registries() -> None:
    """Enforce at import what the annotations above only document.

    ruff is the only static gate in this repo — there is no mypy — so
    ``dict[str, type[CaseProperty]]`` buys nothing on its own. These assertions are
    what actually stop a class missing ``check`` from being registered as a case
    property, or a deferral pointing at a name no property provides. Import time is
    the right moment: it costs nothing and fires before any hardware is touched.
    """
    for registry, protocol in (
        (CASE_PROPERTY_REGISTRY, CaseProperty),
        (GROUP_PROPERTY_REGISTRY, GroupProperty),
    ):
        for key, cls in registry.items():
            instance = cls()
            if not isinstance(instance, protocol):
                msg = f"{cls.__name__} does not satisfy {protocol.__name__}"
                raise TypeError(msg)
            if instance.name != key:
                msg = f"registry key {key!r} does not match {cls.__name__}.name {instance.name!r}"
                raise ValueError(msg)
            target = instance.defers_nonfinite_to
            if target and target not in CASE_PROPERTY_REGISTRY:
                msg = (
                    f"{cls.__name__} defers non-finite output to {target!r}, which is "
                    f"not a registered case property"
                )
                raise ValueError(msg)

158	            msg = (

206	class ReferenceOracle:
207	    """One property: the output matches a trusted recomputation of it.
208	
209	    The strongest arm, and the brittlest. It needs three things the declarative arm
210	    does not — a reference implementation, a threshold, and an output dtype that has
211	    a unit roundoff — and where any of them is missing it must say INCONCLUSIVE
212	    rather than guess. Each such path is a *reduction in this arm's measured power*,
213	    which is exactly what the comparison is trying to quantify, so none of them may
214	    be quietly rounded to PASS or FAIL.
215	
216	    ``reference_fn`` is called as ``reference_fn(**kernel_inputs(case))``, so it is
217	    written with the kernel's own parameter names and never sees generator
218	    bookkeeping tensors.
219	
220	    A defect in the reference is a defect in the *harness*, and this arm distinguishes
221	    two kinds of it, because they need opposite handling.
222	
223	    An exception propagates. It is unambiguous, it cannot be confused with a finding
224	    about the kernel, and swallowing it would let a wholly broken reference reduce
225	    this arm to a silent no-op across an entire run.
226	
227	    A reference that returns *unusable data* — NaN, an overflowed infinity — does not
228	    raise, and left unchecked it is far more dangerous than the exception.
229	    ``residual_ratio`` answers ``inf``, which is a FAIL, so a perfectly correct kernel
230	    is booked as a caught bug and the detail string names the kernel: a false positive
231	    in the headline metric, manufactured by the harness. The reference's output is
232	    therefore validated before it is compared, and a non-finite one is INCONCLUSIVE
233	    with a detail that says the reference is at fault. Note the asymmetry with a
234	    non-finite *kernel* output, which still FAILs — that one is evidence. A shape
235	    disagreement is a third case again and is handled differently; see ``_check``.
236	
237	    The reference call is wrapped in ``np.errstate(all="ignore")`` for the same
238	    reason. This project sets ``filterwarnings = ["error"]``, which turns a numpy
239	    overflow inside the reference into a raised exception — so the same reference
240	    defect would abort under test config and silently FAIL under production config, in
241	    a project whose central claim is that arms are scored over identical executions.
242	    Aborting is also the wrong failure mode for an offline scoring pass: the pass is
243	    cheap to re-run, but it dies partway through and discards the *already paid for*
244	    hardware time in the rest of the table. Suppressed here and caught by the
245	    finiteness check below, an overflowing reference costs one INCONCLUSIVE row.
246	
247	    ``n`` overrides the accumulation length the test ratio normalizes by; see
248	    ``_accumulation_length``.
249	    """
250	
251	    name = "reference"
252	
253	    def __init__(
254	        self,
255	        reference_fn: Callable[..., np.ndarray],
256	        thresh: float = DEFAULT_THRESH,
257	        n: int | None = None,
258	    ) -> None:
259	        self.reference_fn = reference_fn
260	        self.thresh = thresh
261	        self.n = n
262	
263	    def evaluate(self, rows: list[ExecutionResult]) -> list[PropertyResult]:
264	        _require_rows(self.name, rows)
265	        return [self._check(row) for row in rows]
266	
267	    def _result(self, verdict: Verdict, detail: str, case_id: str) -> PropertyResult:
268	        """Every result this arm emits, built in one place.
269	
270	        Centralized so ``case_id`` cannot be forgotten on one branch out of five.
271	        The reference arm is per-row, so it always attributes to the case; there is
272	        no group-scoped path here to get wrong.
273	        """
274	        _require_case_id(self.name, case_id)
275	        return PropertyResult(
276	            property_name=REFERENCE_PROPERTY,
277	            tier=TIER_PORTABLE,
278	            # A recomputation is compared through a numerical threshold, so this arm
279	            # is definitionally not tolerance-free. That is the whole contrast the
280	            # headline claim draws against the structural declarative properties.
281	            tolerance_free=False,
282	            verdict=verdict,
283	            detail=detail,
284	            case_id=case_id,
285	        )
286	
287	    def _length(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> int:
288	        """The accumulation length the test ratio normalizes by.
289	
290	        Taken from the *input*, not the output. The output's last axis is only the
291	        accumulation length for a full-shape elementwise kernel; for anything that
292	        reduces, it is the shape the error was reduced *into*, which is exactly the
293	        trap ``RowsSumToOne`` documents one module over. Measured on correct float32
294	        reductions, normalizing by the output's last axis is 18x too strict for a
295	        row-wise reduction of shape (2, 262144) -> (2,) and 12x too strict for a full
296	        512x4096 reduction -> (1,), because ``log2(2)`` and ``log2(1)`` replace
297	        ``log2(262144)`` and ``log2(4096)``. Over-normalizing is not a safety margin:
298	        it raises the pass/fail line against a correct kernel until the arm books it
299	        as a caught bug.
300	
301	        ``Case.shape`` describes the primary input ``x``, so its last axis is the
302	        reduction length for this corpus's row-wise kernels — the same restriction
303	        ``residual_ratio``'s own default carries, moved to the side of the comparison
304	        where it actually holds. A contraction length that is not an input dimension
305	        either (GEMM's K) is not derivable here at all; that is what ``n`` on the
306	        constructor is for.
307	
308	        A scalar input has no last axis and a zero-length one is not a valid
309	        accumulation, so both fall back to 1, which ``residual_ratio`` floors to a
310	        divisor of 1.0 — no length normalization at all. That is the conservative
311	        direction: it cannot manufacture a pass, and it keeps a degenerate shape from
312	        reaching ``_validate_n``, which rejects ``n < 1`` with a bare ValueError that
313	        would abort the whole scoring pass over one row.
314	        """
315	        if self.n is not None:
316	            return self.n
317	        shape = row.case.shape
318	        return shape[-1] if shape and shape[-1] >= 1 else 1
319	
320	    def _check(self, row: ExecutionResult) -> PropertyResult:
321	        case_id = row.case.case_id
322	        # Status and output presence are independent conditions; a Phase 3 timeout
323	        # can leave a partially written buffer behind, so both are checked.
324	        if row.status != Status.OK:
325	            return self._result(Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, f"status={row.status!r}", case_id)
326	        if OUTPUT_NAME not in row.outputs:
327	            detail = f"missing output {OUTPUT_NAME!r}"
328	            return self._result(Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id)
329	
330	        # atleast_1d for the same reason residual_ratio applies it: a 0-d output would
331	        # make `.shape[-1]` an IndexError. `single_output` normalizes this at the
332	        # execution boundary, so it should be unreachable — but so is a zero-size
333	        # output, which is guarded two lines down, and this is the same class of
334	        # defensiveness at the same cost.
335	        got = np.atleast_1d(row.outputs[OUTPUT_NAME])
336	        if got.size == 0:
337	            # Agreement over zero elements is vacuously true, not evidence. It also
338	            # cannot be measured: residual_ratio answers NaN, which is a non-pass and
339	            # so a FAIL if taken at face value.
340	            return self._result(Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EMPTY_DETAIL, case_id)
341	
342	        # See the class docstring: suppressed so that an overflowing reference is one
343	        # INCONCLUSIVE row rather than a run-aborting exception under test config and
344	        # a silent FAIL under production config.
345	        try:
346	            with np.errstate(all="ignore"):
347	                expected = np.atleast_1d(
348	                    np.asarray(self.reference_fn(**kernel_inputs(row.case)))
349	                )
350	        except ReferenceUnavailable as exc:
351	            return self._result(Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, str(exc), case_id)
352	
353	        # Validate the reference before comparing against it. residual_ratio answers
354	        # inf for a non-finite reference, and inf is a FAIL — so an unchecked reference
355	        # defect books a *correct* kernel as a caught bug, with a detail naming the
356	        # kernel. That is a false positive manufactured by the harness, in the one
357	        # number this project reports. Non-finite is unambiguously the reference's
358	        # fault: it is computed from a recorded input by trusted code, so NaN or an
359	        # overflowed infinity there is never evidence about the kernel.
360	        if expected.dtype.kind in "fc" and not np.all(np.isfinite(expected)):
361	            detail = "reference output is non-finite; the reference, not the kernel"
362	            return self._result(Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, detail, case_id)
363	
364	        # A shape disagreement is deliberately NOT treated the same way, because it is
365	        # symmetric: nothing here knows the correct output shape independently, so
366	        # "reference is wrong" and "kernel returned the wrong shape" are the same
367	        # observation. Calling it INCONCLUSIVE would permanently blind the strong arm
368	        # to wrong-shaped output, which is a common and serious real kernel bug and
369	        # exactly what this arm exists to catch. The two error sources are also very
370	        # differently detectable: a mis-written reference disagrees on *every* row, so
371	        # it shows up as a 100% failure rate including against the reference kernel
372	        # itself, whereas the non-finite case above is data-dependent and intermittent
373	        # (reachable on ~9.5% of groups at the default ShiftRows shift scale) and so
374	        # would hide inside a plausible-looking detection rate. FAIL is therefore the
375	        # right verdict; what the harness owes the reader is a detail that names both
376	        # shapes and does not pretend to know which side is wrong.
377	        if expected.shape != got.shape:
378	            detail = (
379	                f"shape mismatch: output {got.shape} vs reference {expected.shape} "
380	                f"(one of the two is wrong; this arm cannot tell which)"
381	            )
382	            return self._result(Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id)
383	
384	        try:
385	            # dtype= comes from the recorded output, not the reference: the reference
386	            # may be computed at higher precision, and the rounding budget belongs to
387	            # the dtype the kernel actually produced.
388	            ratio = residual_ratio(
389	                got, expected, dtype=got.dtype, n=self._length(row)
390	            )
391	        except ExactDtypeError:
392	            # PERSISTABLE_KINDS is "biuf", so int and bool outputs genuinely arrive
393	            # here. A test ratio is undefined for them: FAIL would book a possibly
394	            # correct integer kernel as a caught bug — a false positive injected
395	            # straight into the headline metric — and letting the exception escape
396	            # would abort a run whose hardware time cannot be recovered.
397	            return self._result(Verdict.INCONCLUSIVE, _EXACT_DTYPE_DETAIL, case_id)
398	
399	        if not within_threshold(ratio, self.thresh):
400	            detail = f"reference test ratio {ratio:.3g} >= {self.thresh}"
401	            return self._result(Verdict.FAIL, detail, case_id)
402	        return self._result(Verdict.PASS, f"ratio={ratio:.3g}", case_id)

411	    ratio precisely so it would not be a strawman — but that strengthening is only
412	    credible if a reader can see what the *unstrengthened* version scores on the very
413	    same executions. Phase 1 measured the two as agreeing on float32 softmax at
414	    n=4096; carrying this arm turns that measurement into something auditable rather
415	    than something to be taken on trust.
416	
417	    So this arm is not tuned, and must not become tuned. ``rtol`` and ``atol`` are
418	    numpy's documented defaults, pinned by a test. Improving it would delete the
419	    comparison it exists to provide.

422	    reasons — see that class for the full argument:
423	
424	    * an exception from the reference propagates;
425	    * a non-finite reference output is INCONCLUSIVE naming the reference, because
426	      ``allclose`` against NaN is False and would otherwise manufacture a false
427	      positive out of a broken reference;
428	    * a shape disagreement is FAIL, not INCONCLUSIVE, because nothing here knows the
429	      correct shape independently and blinding the arm to wrong-shaped output would
430	      hide a common real kernel bug. ``np.allclose`` *broadcasts*, so this check is
431	      load-bearing rather than defensive: (2,3) against (2,1) would otherwise compare

462	        """

465	            property_name=ALLCLOSE_PROPERTY,
466	            tier=TIER_PORTABLE,
467	            # A tolerance is the entire mechanism. This arm is the definition of

470	            tolerance_free=False,

494	        # Suppressed for the reason ReferenceOracle suppresses it: this project sets

499	            with np.errstate(all="ignore"):

528	    together and has no meaning applied to either alone.
529	
530	    The property set is validated at construction rather than at first use, so a
531	    misconfigured set fails before any evaluation runs — the failure mode it guards
532	    against is silent, and a silent miss discovered after the numbers are reported is
533	    not discovered at all.

538	    def __init__(

540	        case_properties: Iterable[CaseProperty],
541	        group_properties: Iterable[GroupProperty] = (),
542	    ) -> None:

544	        self.group_properties = tuple(group_properties)
545	        validate_property_set([*self.case_properties, *self.group_properties])
546	
547	    def evaluate(self, rows: list[ExecutionResult]) -> list[PropertyResult]:
548	        _require_rows(self.name, rows)

550	        results.extend(prop.check_group(rows) for prop in self.group_properties)
551	        return results

554	class HybridOracle:
555	    """Laws first as a cheap filter, the reference recompute only if they find nothing.
556	
557	    The precedence is the point. A reference recompute costs a full evaluation of the
558	    kernel's semantics in the harness; the declarative laws are elementwise scans and
559	    one reduction. So when the laws already reached FAIL, the reference arm can add

577	    reference-arm coverage is *conditional*: on a declarative-FAIL group it never

579	    table that is harmless — the group was caught either way — but any per-property

586	    disagree with it.

589	    name = "hybrid"

592	        self.declarative = declarative
593	        self.reference = reference
